newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit seen staying soft on trade deficit rumour.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit seen staying soft on trade deficit rumour.

text.p: * Ringgit seen staying soft on rumour of April trade deficit
* Fear of central bank intervention to cap dollar/ringgit upside at 2.5200
The ringgit barely moved against the U.S. dollar in early Asian trading, but its undertone was expected to remain soft amid talk of a large April trade deficit, dealers said.
"The market is talking about a one- to two-billion-ringgit deficit for April and this will continue to pressure the ringgit," said a dealer at a large Malaysian bank.
Malaysia posted a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March.
But immediate upside for the dollar/ringgit was likely to be capped at 2.5190/5200 due to fears of central bank intervention.
Dealers said they also expected heavy offers of dollar/ringgit from local players at 2.5200.
Tight trading in the dollar/majors was also limiting dollar/ringgit movements.
Dealers said the market was also awaiting April monetary supply figures, which could provide some clues to the country's interest rate direction.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5169/79 a dollar against 2.5160/70 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
